subject: Routing hint header not propagating through SDK — demo + mitigation ask
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie@brightlane.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — routing behaviour and logs

Thanks Sophie — quick recap from today. During the demo we saw 2x requests where Brightlane's routing preference (X-BL-Variant) was not honored and the call fell back to a default model variant. You captured the repro and shared the recording, and I attached the trimmed server log (brightlane-reqs.log) with the exact request ids.

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether you can reliably repro this on your side (same request ids are in the log)? If yes, would you be open to a short shared screen tomorrow so our runtime team can see the trace live?

Next steps I propose:
- I will loop in Redwood runtime (logan, sean) and product (marissa) so we can triage.
- If it's an SDK propagation issue, we can push a short-term gateway header mapping while we ship an SDK flag to expose X-BL-Variant.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — that bug is blocking your canary.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — routing behaviour and logs

Thanks Vanessa — yes, we repro'd twice after the call. Excerpts from our QA run:
- Request 20261003-11:01:45: header X-BL-Variant=beta present at client but absent at the Redwood proxy (see log lines 234-240).
- Request 20261003-11:05:02: similar drop, different client instance.

We recorded the Chrome devtools and attached the trimmed video. Our short-term ask: if Redwood can honor a header mapping (for now map X-BL-Variant -> X-Redwood-Routing-Hint) that would let us complete canary. Long-term we'd prefer the SDK to expose the variant header consistently.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Tran, Technical Program Manager
Brightlane, Inc.

Date: 2026-10-04T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Demo follow-up — routing behaviour and logs

Looping you in — Brightlane is seeing their client header (X-BL-Variant) disappear before the proxy/runtime sees it. They can repro, and their immediate request is a temporary header mapping so routing works for their canary.

What I tried so far: verified the log lines they sent, asked them for a short screen share. From a sales perspective the priority is: unblock canary by EOD Friday, then ship a robust SDK flag so the header is passed under instrumented conditions (we have security concerns around allowing arbitrary headers by default).

Questions for runtime/product:
1) Can gateway do a mapping rule that renames X-BL-Variant -> X-Redwood-Routing-Hint for Brightlane traffic only? Risk?
2) If this is an SDK client propagation bug, how long to ship a small boolean flag (propagate_client_hint) that opts-in?
3) Do we need a temporary signed config or will an env-based mapping suffice?

Happy to set up a triage call; Sophie is available 10/04 14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo follow-up — routing behaviour and logs

Thanks for the details — quick triage notes after looking at brightlane-reqs.log and the demo clip:
- Evidence points to client-side SDK stripping for certain outgoing headers when request uses persistent connection pooling (we saw the client library v1.4.2 with keep-alive behavior in the recording).
- Gateway currently only proxies a safe-list of headers; X-BL-Variant is not on that list which explains the absence server-side.

Proposed fast path (can unblock canary by EOD Friday):
A) Gateway header mapping: add a tenant-scoped mapping that maps incoming X-BL-Variant -> X-Redwood-Routing-Hint. Minimal risk; we already support tenant-scoped header transforms in config. Rollout plan: staging -> prod with feature flag, 2-hour rollout window, and automatic rollback on error. I can get an initial config PR today.

B) Medium-term: SDK change: add a boolean config propagate_client_hint (default false). When true, the SDK will copy X-BL-Variant from outgoing metadata into a proxied header and ensure it survives connection pooling. Estimate: 3 dev days + 1 day for QA and a canary rollout. If we prioritize, we can target a staged release in 2 weeks.

C) Security: require tenants to opt-in to the mapping via console (checkbox) to prevent accidental exposure of arbitrary client-only headers. Product (marissa) — can you confirm UI/console gating?

I also opened ENG-9876 for the SDK change and attached the jira link. Next steps: Vanessa to confirm Brightlane availability for a 10/04 14:00 PT triage; if they prefer, we can do a shorter 20-minute runbook to apply gateway mapping immediately.

— Logan
Principal Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
